notes: Customer is an infra vendor building gateway appliances for telco customers — sensitive latency requirements for chat and live routing
Primary ask: private VPC deployment with strict egress controls, IP allowlists, and KMS integration for model logs and user data
Prefers dedicated control plane in Redwood Private but must ensure data never leaves us-east-1 region for EU customers' tenants (data residency requirement)
Infosec quote: 'We need cryptographic separation of keys and ability to rotate without downtime'
SE note: exploring PrivateLink because customer cannot accept VPC peering across accounts due to routing constraints in their environment
Customer wants per-request audit entries exported to their SIEM (Splunk) and S3 with 7-year retention for compliance
Cost sensitivity: medium — willing to pay premium for audited, private deployment but wants Optimize recommendations to reduce token cost
Model preference: Mistral-family open models and a quantized 8-bit variant for cost/latency tradeoffs; fallback to smaller model if latency spikes
Latency/throughput targets: p50 < 80ms for short chat turns, sustained throughput 600 reqs/min for reranking pipelines
Egress model: outbound calls must go through NAT gateway and a proxy with allowlist of Redwood egress IPs; no direct internet egress from compute subnets
Firewall rules: default deny, only allow TLS to Redwood endpoint on specific ports; customer will provide NGFW ACLs and expects Redwood to document required ports and CIDRs
KMS integration: customer requests customer-managed keys (AWS KMS) with key alias pattern 'mistral/redwood/*' and schema for key rotation events
Audit logging: want structured audit logs (JSON) including request_id, model_version, prompt_hash (sha256), response_checksum, and encryption-key-id
Data residency: tenant data must be stored in us-east-1; backups snapshot policy must be explicated; customer requires certificate of deletion for test data after POC
Blocker observed: legal wants SOC2 Type II and latest pen test report from Redwood before signing SOW
network_requirements: Private connectivity: prefer AWS PrivateLink endpoint in customer VPC; fallback plan: VPC peering with strict route table controls
IP allowlist: customer will provide /24 blocks for their outbound proxies to be whitelisted by Redwood (two subnets: 10.12.34.0/24, 10.12.35.0/24)
Egress controls: all outbound traffic must route via customer-managed NAT + proxy; Redwood must provide egress IPs and FQDNs for allowlist
Firewall requirements: stateful NGFW with TLS interception prohibited; mutual TLS support required between customer proxy and Redwood endpoint
Port matrix: only TCP 443 to PrivateLink endpoint; internal health checks on 8000-8010 over PrivateLink for metrics (customer asked to minimize open ports)
VPC flow logs: customer requires flow logs to be enabled and delivered to their central S3 bucket and Splunk; Redwood must share expected flow log fields
Peering constraints: no transitive routing allowed; clear route table entries and no overlapping CIDRs with customer control plane
Bastion/proxy rules: management plane access limited to customer-maintained bastion host IPs; Redwood ops to use customer-supplied jump host when needed
poc_details: Requested POC length: 14 days in dedicated VPC with PrivateLink
POC goals: validate latency SLOs, verify KMS envelope encryption integration, prove audit log pipeline into Splunk
Provisioning items: PrivateLink endpoint, peering fallback, customer KMS key, S3 audit bucket (us-east-1), SIEM ingest credentials
Success criteria: p50 latency <= 80ms for chat; end-to-end encrypted logs into S3 and visible in Splunk; documented key rotation with zero-data-loss
Rollback plan: immediate suspension of POC and deletion of test data on failed security sign-off; certificate of deletion to be provided
compliance_documents_requested: Data processing addendum (DPA) with explicit residency clauses
KMS architecture diagram and key rotation policy
